**Sundhedsklynge Byen** is a local healthcare cluster (sundhedsklynge) operating within [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] in Denmark [^src5]. It is one of the organizational units monitored in the national clinical quality databases and annual reports for [[atrieflimren|atrieflimren]] (atrial fibrillation), managed by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) and Sundhedsvæsenets Kvalitetsinstitut. 

The cluster's primary significance in the corpus relates to its performance on national healthcare quality standards. For Indikator 1, which measures the timely initiation of anticoagulation therapy for newly diagnosed patients, Sundhedsklynge Byen recorded a compliance rate of 88.5% [^src1]. This result is notable because it fails to meet the stringent national standard of 90% [^src1]. In broader geographic analyses of treatment coverage, Sundhedsklynge Byen is identified among the clusters with the lowest performance levels, hovering around 85%, while several clusters in North and Central Jutland successfully meet the development targets [^src9]. 

Beyond anticoagulation initiation, the cluster's clinical outcomes and treatment persistence are rigorously tracked across multiple indicators. It is included in national geographic distributions for [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]], which measures the incidence of ischemic stroke (apopleksi) among atrial fibrillation patients [^src4]. Furthermore, the cluster's data is continuously evaluated for long-term treatment coverage (2-year and 5-year persistence), annual kidney function monitoring (P-creatinine), severe bleeding events, heart failure development, and mortality rates [^src2] [^src3] [^src4] [^src6] [^src7] [^src10] [^src12]. These metrics allow regional and national health authorities to benchmark Sundhedsklynge Byen against other units, such as [[sundhedsklynge-bornholm|Sundhedsklynge Bornholm]] and [[sundhedsklynge-midt|Sundhedsklynge Midt]], to identify variations in clinical practice and target quality improvement initiatives [^src4].
